summary: Latvia's Interior Ministry reports child victims by offence and sex, and says 4% of identified suspects of sexual offences against minors were foreign citizens; trafficking victims are split into Latvian and third-country nationals. That is a citizenship proxy only. Ethnicity (tautība), including the large Russian minority, is not recorded in crime data.

nations.National (Interior Ministry, IDC): Annual report on juvenile crime and child victims; crime-register tables.

european_title: Not recorded by any Latvian crime source
european_note: Latvian crime records hold citizenship (valstiskā piederība), not ethnicity. Russians and other minorities are counted in the population register and census but not in any crime, victim or child-protection statistic, so neither ethnic Europeans nor any ethnic group can be measured for child harm.
proxy_note: Latvia records citizenship only in crime data, never ethnicity. Every group below is a proxy, not ethnicity.

harms.label: Sexual offences against minors
harms.intro: In 2025, 40 children were victims of rape and 118 of sexual violence (Interior Ministry). 4% of identified suspects of sexual offences against minors were citizens of other countries (Uzbekistan, Russia, Lithuania, Ukraine); 21% of suspects were themselves minors. Victims have no citizenship.

victims.text: Child victims are counted by sex, age and municipality; no citizenship.

Citizenship, a proxy, not ethnicity: Latvian nationals include citizens and non-citizens (mostly ethnic Russians and other Soviet-era residents); ethnicity (tautība) is not recorded in crime data.

harms.intro: 47 children were victims of pornography offences (Art. 166) in 2025. These offences are part of the sexual offences against minors for which 4% of identified suspects were foreign citizens.

Citizenship, a proxy, not ethnicity: Latvian nationals include citizens and non-citizens (mostly ethnic Russians and other Soviet-era residents); ethnicity (tautība) is not recorded in crime data. breakdown.why: The Interior Ministry's 2025 report on juvenile crime and child victims says 4% of identified suspects of sexual offences against minors were citizens of other countries (Uzbekistan, Russia, Lithuania, Ukraine); the number of suspects is not given. Child victims (40 of rape, 118 of sexual violence) have sex but no citizenship.

The same report counts 184 child victims of cruelty and violence against a minor (Art. 174) and 663 child victims of all offences in 2025, by sex and municipality only. The Interior Ministry's digital centre (IDC) tables of victims and accused give sex and age, no citizenship.
Children's-rights violations (2,994 administrative cases in 2025) are counted without citizenship or ethnicity.
Child victims of murder (2) and aggravated murder (8) in 2025 have sex only; no citizenship.

The Interior Ministry identified 22 trafficking victims in 2025: 11 Latvian nationals and 11 third-country nationals (all ages). The child-victim table records no child victims of trafficking (Art. 154.1) in 2025. No trafficker citizenship.
Child pornography offences (Art. 166) are inside the sexual offences against minors for which 4% of identified suspects were foreign citizens. No victims by citizenship.

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify ethnic European children (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump ethnic Europeans with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, ethnic Europeans separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies ethnic Europeans, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when ethnic European children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points (victims 37.5, perpetrators 37.5); coverage, rates and access share the other 25. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points. A country with no real ethnicity data for victims or perpetrators is capped at 25%.
score.why: Latvia scores 10% on the stricter scale (0-20%). The Interior Ministry gives the share of foreign citizens among suspects of sexual offences against minors (4%) and trafficking victims as Latvian or third-country nationals. Child victims have no citizenship, and no ethnicity is recorded.
score.weights_id: harm weights of 19 Nov 2026 (homicide 25, sexual abuse 20, sex trafficking 20, physical abuse 15, online exploitation 10, neglect 10)
